name: St. Kitts and Nevis
headline: St. Kitts and Nevis: +1.5% growth in 2025, 0.8% inflation, debt 59% of GDP
sections: St. Kitts and Nevis is a $1.1 billion economy (2025), the world's 204th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +1.5% in 2025, slower than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $37K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 4.0% of GDP (2025).
Consumer prices rose 0.8% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges, down from 2.7% in 2022.
Gross government debt is 59% of GDP (2025), a moderate level that has fallen from 72% in 2020. The general government balance is −11.8% of GDP (2025), a deficit beyond the common 3% benchmark.
The current account balance is −14.4% of GDP (2025), a sizeable external financing need. Net FDI inflows were 2.4% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 79% of GDP by 2031, still rising from today's level. Life expectancy is 72.3 years (2024). Population: 52 thousand (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
